items.stem: Which OPT phase is the appropriate starting point for a previously sedentary client?

options.rationale: Correct: NASM's OPT model begins new/deconditioned clients in stabilisation endurance to build control and joint stability.
Power is an advanced phase, not a starting point for a sedentary client.
Maximal strength requires a foundation built in earlier phases.
Hypertrophy work comes after a stabilisation base.

items.stem: During an overhead squat assessment, the client's knees move inward. Which muscles are most likely overactive?

options.rationale: Correct: knees caving in (valgus) commonly reflects overactive adductors and underactive gluteus medius/maximus.
The biceps are not implicated in knee valgus during a squat.
Wrist flexors are unrelated to knee movement.

options.text: The calves only, with no hip involvement
options.rationale: Knee valgus is primarily a hip/adductor issue, not calves alone.

items.explanation: Correct: knees caving in (valgus) commonly reflects overactive adductors and underactive gluteus medius/maximus.

items.stem: Which TWO actions fall WITHIN a certified personal trainer's scope of practice?

options.text: Designing and progressing a safe exercise program
options.rationale: Correct: program design and progression are core trainer responsibilities.
Correct: general healthy-eating guidance is within scope; detailed medical nutrition therapy is not.
Diagnosis is outside a trainer's scope and belongs to licensed clinicians.

options.text: Prescribing a therapeutic diet for a disease
options.rationale: Medical nutrition therapy requires a registered dietitian/clinician.

items.explanation: Correct: program design and progression are core trainer responsibilities.
